facts.raw_span: an 18-month history of erythroderma affecting his entire body and face
slightly pruritic, slowly progressive erythematous lesions on his trunk and retroauricular area
confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques with overlying thick greasy scales on the face, neck, trunk, genitalia, upper and lower extremities, palms, and soles
sparing of the nails and scalp
bilateral lower‐lid ectropion was present
no palpable lymphadenopathy
epidermotropism of a large number of atypical lymphocytes—single and in clusters
a superficial dermal band‐like lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal fibrosis
Direct immunofluorescence was negative for fibrinogen, C3, IgA, IgM, and IgG
tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO but negative for CD4, CD8, and CD7
CD30 was positive in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of erythroderma, confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques, and epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes is consistent with Mycosis fungoides, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

The patient's presentation of erythroderma, bilateral lower-lid ectropion, and CD30 positivity in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes is consistent with Sezary syndrome, an aggressive form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

The patient's initial presentation of slightly pruritic, slowly progressive erythematous lesions on the trunk and retroauricular area, and the presence of confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques, could be consistent with psoriasis, although the subsequent development of erythroderma and lymphocytic infiltrate suggests a more complex diagnosis.

The patient's initial presentation of slightly pruritic, slowly progressive erythematous lesions on the trunk and retroauricular area could be consistent with atopic dermatitis, although the subsequent development of erythroderma and lymphocytic infiltrate suggests a more complex diagnosis.

The patient's presentation of epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and a superficial dermal band-like lymphocytic infiltrate could be consistent with cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia, a condition characterized by an abnormal immune response.
The patient's presentation of erythroderma could be consistent with a drug-induced reaction, given the history of multiple courses of oral prednisolone and cyclosporine.

The patient's presentation of congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma and the presence of confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques could be consistent with Netherton syndrome, a rare genetic disorder.

The patient's presentation of epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and CD30 positivity in fewer than 25% of lymphocytes could be consistent with lymphomatoid papulosis, a condition characterized by a mixture of lymphomatous and inflammatory features.
It explains the presence of bilateral lower-lid ectropion and atypical lymphocytes in skin punch biopsies.
